record_type_quote: The current study aims to replicate and extend Martin’s (1978) second study with two key improvements: a larger, diverse sample to enhance generalizability and modernized testing procedures.

targets.title: Memory span as a measure of individual differences in memory capacity.
targets.evidence_quote: The current study aims to replicate and extend Martin’s (1978) second study with two key improvements: a larger, diverse sample to enhance generalizability and modernized testing procedures.
targets.outcome_quote: The results obtained in the current study of Martin’s (1978) second experiment are consistent with the hypothesis that digit span is a reliable predictor of other memory tasks. However, our ﬁndings only partially align with those reported by Martin (1978).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly say only partial alignment overall: a digit span/order recall association remains, while the lenient/item-recall association contrasts with the original nonsignificant association. Limitations are not framed as preventing interpretation.

reasoning: New sample of 79 participants directly retests Martin Experiment 2 using adapted online digit span and serial recall tasks. Other memory models and studies supply background, measurement materials, or possible explanations rather than further replication targets.
